lead: Louisville plumbing deals with old Victorian homes, river flooding, hard water and cold snaps. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Louisville.
risk: aging pipes in older homes, basement backups and frozen pipes
risk_short: old pipes, basement backups and frozen pipes
why: Old Louisville, the Highlands, Germantown and Crescent Hill have homes from the late 1800s and early 1900s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals.
Heavy rain overloads older sewers and backs water into basements. Cold snaps freeze pipes in exterior walls and crawl spaces.
water: Louisville Water draws from the Ohio River, partly through riverbank filtration. The water is moderately hard.
tips: Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in Old Louisville, the Highlands, Germantown, Crescent Hill, Clifton, Butchertown and every other Louisville neighborhood.
permits: Kentucky's Division of Plumbing licenses plumbers and oversees plumbing permits and inspections across the state, including Louisville.

faq.a: Kentucky licenses plumbers statewide through the Division of Plumbing in the Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction. Ask for the license number before work starts.
